[ Project S - Hello_World ]
​
Update = 10.09.24
​
This is meant to be a sudo dev log / Suggestions intake forum for my new project. I aim to log my process, add some accountability, and ask for positive feedback from more veteran game devs. I am new to RPG Maker and new to game development. I am more comfortable with Python coding and using Godot, but I decided to take on RPG maker to kick-start my prototype before I invest too much time in a game that might not work.
Now, due to my glorious ADHD, I lack focus and have a love-hate relationship with structure. I am already jumping around in my "Timeline." It's mainly there to give me goals and set deadlines; without this, my ADHD brain will not work.  Also, it is a way to let possible big-brained individuals know where they can focus on their suggestions and feedback
.
​
P.S. This post is too long. Sorry.
​
6-Month Prototype Development Timeline (October 2024 – April 2025)
*Crosses fingers*
​
Spoiler:
Projected Timeline
1.
Worldbuilding & Narrative Structure (October 4 – October 25, 2024)  <--- Current Focus
Goals:
Draft the game’s world and establish the central conflict
.
<--- Decided core aspects; need feedback here.
Define the protagonist’s role and start working on critical characters
. <--- Decided core aspects; need feedback here.
Draft the first few chapters of the story.
<--- Currently working here
Milestone Date:
October 25, 2024
​
2. Character Design and Relationships (October 26 – November 15, 2024)
Goals:
Complete initial designs for 3-5 main characters (backstory, personality, visual sketches).
<-- No visuals yet. Have bases for the main 5 Characters. Drafts on side/optional characters.
Develop recruitment stories and relationship mechanics.
Milestone Date:
November 15, 2024
​
3. Core Mechanics & Systems (November 16 – January 6, 2025)
Goals:
Develop foundational systems for character recruitment, party management, and bonding.
Implement a basic inventory and customization system. <--- Working on this  - 10.05
Start early event scripting for character moments (side quests, interactions).
Milestone Date:
January 6, 2025
Note:
This is a two-part phase. The first half will focus on building the underlying systems (November 16 – December 15), while the second half will be used for refining and iterating on the systems (December 16 – January 6).
​
4. Combat System (January 7 – March 1, 2025)
Goals:
Create a basic combat system that highlights party roles and character synergy.  <--- I Fine-tuned and decided to simplify the battle mechanics a bit; felt too complicated for non-hardcore strategy people.  - 10.06
Design combat encounters using the characters’ unique abilities. <--- Started -  Working on Skills - 10.05
Balance combat dynamics to integrate relationships and party mechanics.  <--- Started  - 10.05
Milestone Date:
March 1, 2025
Note:
While early combat mechanics will begin earlier, this phase focuses heavily on refining, testing, and balancing the system.
​
5. Early Storyboarding & Event Scripting (January 7 – March 1, 2025)
Goals:
Outline and script the first few chapters, with key character-driven events.
Implement side quests and bonding moments that reveal character growth.
Create cutscenes and events that drive character development.
Milestone Date:
March 1, 2025
Note:
This phase overlaps with combat system development, allowing both narrative and gameplay to evolve in tandem.
​
6. Playtesting & Feedback Collection (March 2 – April 1, 2025)
Goals:
Conduct playtests of the character interactions, combat, and relationship systems.
Gather player feedback on character engagement, story, and mechanics.
Refine systems based on feedback, fixing bugs and improving the flow of character development.
Milestone Date:
April 1, 2025
​
Prototype Completion: April 4, 2025
By
April 4, 2025
, you should have a functional prototype that showcases:
Character interactions, relationships, and basic bonding systems.
A combat system where players can feel the impact of party dynamics.
The first few hours of the story, including the introduction of the main characters and core conflict.
The ability to explore a small world or base, recruit characters, and start forming your party.
​
Quick Summary
​
The game is set in a high fantasy MMO where the player controls a character navigating both the in-game world and their relationships. The MMO serves as a backdrop for a story focused on personal growth, self-acceptance, and character-driven conflict. The game follows a lighthearted, fun tone, akin to sports anime, with moments of drama arising from interpersonal dynamics rather than world-shaking events.
In the MMO, players form guilds, complete quests, and develop relationships with both other players and AI-driven NPCs. The protagonist’s guild grows over time, reflecting their personal journey, as they recruit new members and gain in-game advantages like buffs and guild-specific resources. Outside the game, real-world influences (such as media, developers, and celebrity gamers) subtly shape how the MMO and its community evolve, though the story remains focused on the personal experiences within the game.
​
Spoiler:
Project Summary
​
Project Summary
Genre & Tone: High fantasy MMO, character-driven story with a sports anime vibe.
Major Factions: Player guilds, game developers, media influencers, AI NPCs.
Cultural Structures: Modern-day real world, traditional MMO fantasy world.
World State: Well-established MMO, real-world influences present but light.
Key Locations: Starting Town, Guild Hall, Starter Zones (Forest, Plains, Hills, Lake).
Magic/Technology: D&D-inspired magic system, potential for customizable spells.
Focus: Character growth, relationships, lighthearted conflict with moments of drama.
World Overview Guide
1. Genre & Tone
Genre:
The game is set in a high fantasy MMO where players and NPCs interact in a highly immersive virtual world. The MMO's setting is inspired by D&D-like environments with traditional fantasy elements (magic, guilds, quests, etc.). Outside the game, the real world subtly influences events, though there’s no direct real-world gameplay.
Tone:
The game has a character-driven, lighthearted tone similar to a sports anime. It focuses on personal growth, self-acceptance, and turning new pages in life, with moments of comedy and drama that arise from character interactions and relationships. Rather than grand world-saving missions, the plot revolves around the emotional journeys of the protagonist and their guildmates, both player characters and NPCs.
​
​
2.
Major Factions or Powers
In-Game Factions:
Player Guilds:
Main Character’s Guild: The player forms their own guild, which serves as the centerpiece of both the gameplay and the story. The guild grows over time, gaining unique buffs, resources, and features based on recruited members.
Rival Guilds: There are established guilds within the MMO that provide friendly competition, alliance opportunities, or rivalries. These guilds add complexity to in-game relationships.
NPC Factions:
AI-Driven NPCs: The MMO features sophisticated NPCs who function like players, adding depth to the world. These NPCs have their own motives, relationships, and personalities.
Game World Lore Factions: Traditional fantasy factions (e.g., elves, dwarves, rival kingdoms) that shape the lore of the MMO and may influence gameplay.
Real-World Factions:
Game Developers/Staff:
Developers oversee the MMO and make changes (updates, bug fixes, new content) that affect the in-game world. Occasionally, in-game events may be influenced by developers or their PR team, creating small real-world consequences.
Event Planners: These individuals organize real-world events like tournaments, in-game celebrations, or player meetups that may impact how the game world is perceived or experienced by players.
Media and Influencers:
Streamers, eSports players, and influencers contribute to the MMO’s in-game social dynamics by shaping opinions or creating in-game trends. They can become a subtle force that influences how certain players or guilds are viewed.
​
​
3. Cultural and Social Structures
In the Real World:
The real world remains grounded in modern-day culture, where players use the MMO as an escape or a competitive platform. Real-world societal pressures, such as school, work, relationships, and celebrity culture, will influence players’ behavior and motives in-game.
In the MMO:
The MMO follows the structure of a typical high fantasy world, with a social hierarchy revolving around guilds, quests, and player reputation. Guilds play a central role in in-game politics and player status, and server reputation can influence how players are treated by others.
​
​
4. World’s Current State
In the MMO:
The MMO is a thriving, well-established game with a rich history and evolving narrative. Players can influence the world on a micro-scale by forming guilds, completing quests, and building relationships with NPCs and players alike. However, major world events are typically controlled by developers through game updates and expansions, though player actions can still have smaller-scale impacts (e.g., becoming known within a server or region).
In the Real World:
The real world reacts to the MMO as a popular cultural phenomenon. Events in the game (such as big guild wars, major raids, or the release of new expansions) might cause waves of excitement in the media or among streamers, but these reactions are more reflective than directly influential. The real world is largely a backdrop, grounding the MMO in relatable themes.
​
​
5. Major Locations
In the MMO:
Starting Town:
The entry point for new players. This town contains the essential MMO staples: inns, shops, quest boards, and the guild hall where players can join or create guilds. This is where the protagonist begins their journey and forms their guild.
Main Character’s Guild Hall:
This guild hall starts small but grows over time. Players can customize it as they recruit more members, gaining access to new perks, buffs, resources, and shops. The guild hall is both a gameplay mechanic and a narrative symbol of the protagonist’s growth.
Starter Zone:
The MMO's starter zone is split into several regions designed for new players to explore and learn the game's mechanics:
Forest Map: A wooded area with basic quests and beginner-level enemies.
Plains Map: A wide-open area with simple encounters and resource gathering.
Hills/Mountain Map: A hilly terrain with caves and some elevation-based challenges.
Lake Map: A scenic area with water-based quests, perhaps involving fishing or minor water combat.
In the Real World:
No major gameplay takes place in the real world, but its presence is felt through the in-game dialogue and narrative elements (media, celebrity culture, developers, etc.).
​
​
6. Magic, Technology, or Unique Elements
Magic System:
The game’s magic system is based on the D&D magic rules, with MMO elements such as customizable spells, cooldowns, and resource management (like mana). Players can choose from traditional fantasy classes that rely on a combination of combat, magic, and utility skills.
Unique Element:
One possible unique element could be a customizable spell system, where players can modify the effects of certain spells. NPCs, driven by advanced AI, could use these spells creatively in ways that feel dynamic and unpredictable, adding an extra layer of depth to encounters.
Prototype Focus:
Main Game Loop, Core Characters, and Two Potential Guild Members
​
Core Focus for the Prototype
​
​
Step 1: Define the Main Game Loop
At the heart of any MMO-inspired game lies a core
game loop
that players will engage with consistently. This loop should encompass the central mechanics, narrative beats, and gameplay systems that players will experience throughout the game. For the prototype, we’ll focus on a simplified version of this loop to ensure that the player is always engaged with meaningful actions.
Prototype Main Game Loop:
Exploration
:
The player explores key locations in the MMO world, such as starter zones (e.g., forests, plains, or town hubs).
During exploration, players can encounter
combat opportunities
,
side quests
, and
story-driven events
tied to character growth.
Questing
:
The player takes on
story quests
and
guild-related missions
, advancing both the protagonist’s character arc and guild development.
Quests are a mix of
combat
,
resource gathering
, and
relationship-building
with core characters.
Guild Development
:
As the player completes quests, they unlock small
guild improvements
, helping build out the guild hall. For the prototype, this will be limited to
basic upgrades
, like expanding rooms or adding a small guild feature (no need to implement complex mechanics just yet).
Guild interactions will be primarily focused on the
relationships between the protagonist
and
key guild members
.
Combat
:
The core combat system should be
turn-based or action-based
(depending on your choice), focusing on the protagonist’s
tactical support role
as an Artificer, along with combat from the two initial guild members.
Combat in the prototype will center around
small-scale encounters
, showcasing the team dynamics between the protagonist and guild members.
Character Interactions
:
Between quests and combat, the player can interact with guild members to
advance their relationships
and unlock story-related dialogue or
side missions
.
For the prototype, the focus will be on the interactions with
Guild Member 1
and
Guild Member 2
. Two potential guild members can be briefly introduced, but their mechanics and deeper storylines will remain light for now.
​
Step 2: Flesh Out the Core Characters
For the prototype, we’ll focus on the
protagonist
and two key guild members who will be integral to the main story. These characters should represent the heart of the narrative, and their interactions will help define the emotional tone of the game.
1. Protagonist
Role in the Prototype
:
The protagonist’s main function in the prototype will be to
establish their leadership
role in the guild, as well as their internal struggles with
self-doubt
and
directionlessness
.
The core gameplay loop will show their growth as a leader, starting with initial hesitancy and ending with them taking charge in combat scenarios or guild missions.
In-Game Role
:
The protagonist’s
supportive combat abilities
(e.g., healing, buffing, and tactical planning as an Artificer) will form the foundation of combat encounters in the prototype.
2. Guild Member 1 (The Addicted MMO Veteran)
Introduction
:
This character serves as the
catalyst
for the protagonist’s journey. They will be the first recruit and play a critical role in helping the protagonist form the guild.
The prototype will introduce their
obsession with money
and
in-game exploits
early on, using their questline to teach the player about
resource management
.
Questline Focus
:
Early in the prototype, the player helps Guild Member 1
gather resources
or complete a mission that requires them to use
loopholes
or
in-game strategies
.
Their interactions with the protagonist will highlight the dangers of
using the MMO as an escape
and
chasing external success
without addressing real-world issues.
3. Guild Member 2 (Confident but Lonely Player)
Introduction
:
This guild member will be introduced during the middle of the prototype as a
solo player
who reluctantly joins the protagonist’s guild.
Their initial cold and independent attitude will contrast with the protagonist’s focus on building a community, creating friction.
Questline Focus
:
The prototype will feature an early encounter where the player helps Guild Member 2 tackle a difficult
solo mission
. Over time, they begin to warm up to the idea of working with the guild.
Their story arc in the prototype will begin to reveal their
hidden loneliness
and
need for connection
, though their full emotional growth can be reserved for the final game.
​
Step 3: Introducing Two Potential Guild Members
For the prototype, we’ll introduce
two potential guild members
who hint at the
optional guild member system
, but we won’t fully implement their mechanics or questlines yet. This will give players a taste of what’s to come in the full game without overwhelming development.
Potential Guild Member 1 (The Chef) <<<--- Really enjoy the Idea of a cheff based Character, figuring out a good class to use that is not Cook but more in line with classic MMO class and "flavored" to be a chef/cook. need suggestions.
Introduction
:
This character will be introduced briefly in a town hub or event, where they discuss their desire to open a
restaurant
within a guild.
Their dialogue will hint at the
buffs and stat-boosting meals
they could provide once recruited, but for now, they won’t join the guild or provide the full functionality.
Potential Guild Member 2 (The Martial Artist) <<<--- Not too sold with this concept.
Introduction
:
The player will meet this character during a
PvP event
or
combat-related mission
, where they mention their dream of opening a
Dojo
for training.
Similar to the Chef, they will not join the guild yet, but their
Dojo mechanic
and potential
combat training features
will be hinted at for the full game.
Early Story and Key Events for the Prototype
Here’s a simplified version of the key story events for the prototype, focusing on establishing the main characters and guild mechanics:
1. Guild Formation (Early Game):
[Working on this currently]
The protagonist meets
Guild Member 1
, who convinces them to form a guild. This introduces the
guild mechanic
(recruiting members, managing resources) and serves as the starting point for the protagonist’s leadership journey.
2. Rival Guild Encounter (Mid-Game):
The player encounters a
rival guild
that challenges the protagonist’s team in a
combat scenario
. This highlights the protagonist’s internal struggle with leadership and shows early friction between guild members.
3. Guild Member 2’s Quest (Mid-Game):
The protagonist helps
Guild Member 2
tackle a
solo challenge
, showing the emotional conflict of independence versus teamwork. This event pushes the protagonist to understand the value of supporting others.
4. Final Prototype Mission (Late Game):
The prototype culminates in a
guild-based raid
or
combat scenario
where the protagonist must take full leadership of their team, guiding Guild Members 1 and 2 through a challenging mission. The result should highlight their growth in confidence and leadership.
I have more details and fleshed-out concepts; however, these are the basics. If you want to know more, reach out; PM, carrier pigeon w.e floats thee boat.
Updates:
Spoiler:
DevLog 10.07
Game Dev Log - 10/07/2024
This weekend, I tried to make the most of my free time by focusing heavily on the technical side of the game.
Progress Made
​
Learning JavaScript:
I spent some time learning the basics of JavaScript, and I can see why it's such a popular language compared to Python. While I still find Python more straightforward, JavaScript's flexibility, especially in UI and front-end development, stands out. I’ve already started developing a custom plugin.
Battle Mechanics:
I’ve finalized the basics of the battle mechanics. All character classes are planned, and I’ve developed the skills and abilities for three of these classes up to level 5. I’ve also figured out how to blend the combat styles of Suikoden with D&D, which has been a fun challenge. Originally, I aimed to replicate D&D's class and skill system with a turn-based twist. However, I quickly realized this approach could overwhelm players, especially initially. There were too many options, and it required a solid grasp of D&D mechanics to avoid getting crushed in early encounters.
Simplifying Skills and Combat:
To address this, I’m streamlining the combat system by focusing on two types of skills: basic and class-specific. Instead of bombarding players with too many choices right from the beginning, I’ll gradually introduce more customization as they progress. Players can ease into the complexity without feeling lost or overwhelmed.
Damage Calculations:
I also adjusted the damage formulas, taking inspiration from Pokémon. The damage calculations remain straightforward but have enough depth for those who enjoy min-maxing.
Next Steps:
​
Things are moving at a good pace, and I aim to have a working prototype demo ready soon. Once it's out, I look forward to gathering feedback on the battle mechanics to refine them further.
GameDev Log 10.09.2024
I am enjoying the struggles of RPG Maker. It is a limited but surprisingly powerful tool. I originally wanted to make my prototype with this engine as it would be "quick" to do before investing too much time in a game that won't work. Now... I am thinking about completing the game with RPG Maker.
When coding in Godot, you have nodes that essentially house all the code and parameters of specific things in your game; it can be a Player Character node or a Menu Button. These nodes have different functionalities pre-backed into the engine; for example, a PlayerCharacter node will have pre-determined functions and variables baked in the node that only requires you to call the function/variable.
With RPG maker, the engine itself is comparable to a single node *Granted, this is an exaggeration* however, essentially, the prebaked functions and tools within RPG maker are focused on making RPGs. Godot has multiple kinds of nodes with various functionalities, enabling you to be more flexible in how you go about problem-solving.
The TLTD version of RPG Maker is a single efficient and powerful tool, while Godot is a collection of many different tools designed to take on various functions.
But yeah... this little engine that could makes me happy, and you might be seeing more of me in the future.

Then I figured you're setting your story so the main character is someone
else's
character
in
an MMO. That seems, to someone just reading this description, to be...an unnecessary and confusing intervening layer?
It reads kind of like you're trying to riff off of Sword Art Online, but I'm not sure how successful that is as the premise as a video game. You're trying to entice people to play as someone playing an anime MMO, when they could just...go play an anime MMO
I dunno, see how it goes; there may well be an isekai fanbase who will dig it.
